item.title: Su to Deliver 2025 Arnold Ross Lecture
item.description: Calling all mathematical teens: This lecture is for you! The American Mathematical Society’s 2025 Arnold Ross Lecture will be "Randomness, Geometry, and Privacy," by Francis Su, Harvey Mudd College, on Friday, August 1, 2025, at 11 a.m. PDT at Proof School, San Francisco. The event is free but Zoom attendance requires preregistration before July 31. item.description: Elaine Beebe "My research focuses on numerical algebraic geometry, so this year’s MRC topic, real numerical algebraic geometry, is a perfect fit," said Kisun Lee, a participant at the 2025 Mathematics Research Communities, or MRCs for short. item.title: NSF Invests $74 Million in 6 Mathematical Sciences Research Institutes
item.description: The National Science Foundation (NSF) has announced that it will invest more than $74 million in six U.S. mathematical research institutes. The NSF Mathematical Sciences Research Institutes focus on the mathematical sciences and their broad applications in all fields of science, technology, and many industries, from improving medical care to detecting planets in other solar systems. Each of the selected NSF Mathematical Sciences Research Institutes will receive between $7 million and $17 million

item.title: Giansiracusa to Receive 2026 JPBM Communications Award
item.description: Noah Giansiracusa will receive the 2026 Joint Policy Board for Mathematics (JPBM) Communications Award “for his extraordinary contributions to public understanding of the societal impacts of algorithms through his acclaimed books and influential media presence,” according to the citation. Giansiracusa is an associate professor of mathematics at Bentley University whose second book, Robin Hood Math, was published by Riverhead Books on August 5. item.title: Conquer Algorithms with Robin Hood Math
item.description: Elaine Beebe "Take control of the algorithms that run your life!" is quite a call to action, but Noah Giansiracusa thinks we can do it if we try. The AMS member's second book, Robin Hood Math (Riverhead Books), explores how people of all backgrounds can use the help of math to navigate the increasing hidden complexities of modern life, such as the dark secrets behind Amazon shopping and Google ads. item.title: AMS Appoints Sarah Bryant, PhD, as Chief Scientific Advancement Officer
item.description: The American Mathematical Society (AMS) is happy to announce that Sarah Bryant, PhD, has been promoted to the newly created role of Chief Scientific Advancement Officer (CSAO). Previously Associate Vice President for AMS Office of Programs and Professional Services, Bryant brings more than two decades of experience in mathematics research, education, and leadership to the position. item.title: The Mathematical and Statistical Sciences Annual Survey Reopens
item.description: The Mathematical and Statistical Sciences Annual Survey will reopen on November 12, 2025, inviting mathematics and statistics departments across the country to contribute vital data about the health of the discipline.
